overview: JustBet describes itself as an online sportsbook, racebook and casino. The about page says the company traces its roots to the mid 1990s and that it serves customers in over 56 countries. The sportsbook page says it has been satisfying bettors in more than 100 counties since the 1990s. The word on that page is counties. The two sentences are not the same, and the about page does not name a regulator or a licence.

The house rules say clients must be 18. Handicapper Watchdog's own line is 21. The rules also say JustBet can refuse a wager from anyone, including clients in a state or province that prohibits sports wagering, and that the client is responsible for their own tax reporting.
features: Online or phone wagering. The FAQ says the minimum is $1 online and $100 by phone, and the maximum is up to $20,000 online and up to $20,000 by phone. Higher limits may be granted on request.
House rules price a straight bet at 10/11, which is $110 to win $100, and cap any parlay payout at $150,000.

The house rules say every deposit carries a one time rollover, and that sports, casino, and horse bets all count toward that rollover. If you take a bonus, that one time rollover is replaced by the bonus rollover. A later section says only sports action counts toward a bonus rollover, and that casino and racebook action do not.

Sides, totals, parlays, teasers, if bets, reverses, futures, money lines and buying points. The FAQ also lists NFL halves and quarters, MLB run lines, NHL puck lines and period lines, NBA halves and quarters, college lines, and horse racing win, place, show, daily doubles and exactas.
The homepage also lists live betting, casino games (slots, roulette, video poker) and a racebook.
The site map describes a BetPoints loyalty program that starts when an account is opened.
House rules say bonus offers are optional, have to be taken at the time of deposit, and are available to clients from the US and Canada only. Anonymous proxies are not eligible for bonuses.

pros: The FAQ publishes a minimum and a maximum, and the market list is specific rather than a slogan.
The promotions page says every bonus is optional. If you do not want the rollover, do not enter the code.
The 15% sports offer we could read states the cap, the code, the rollover, and who it excludes.
cons: The about page does not name a licence or a regulator. Outside writeups do not agree on one either, so this page does not invent one.
JustBet's own pages do not agree on the footprint: over 56 countries on the about page, more than 100 counties on the sportsbook page.

The FAQ says crypto payouts can be ready in under 12 hours, one crypto payout a day, and one payout a week by other methods. A later section of the house rules says one payout every 7 days and that requests may take 7 to 15 business days. A credit card deposit requires copies of the card and a photo ID before a withdrawal.
An account with no deposit, withdrawal, or bet for 12 months can be set to a zero balance. The rules say customer service can put a qualified balance back if you ask.
The crypto welcome detail we requested returned page not found, so those rollovers are unpublished on this review.
House rules let the book refuse any wager and change a promotion without notice. Withdrawals can require account validation.
The house age is 18. This site does not treat that as the right line for its readers.
jurisdictions: JustBet says it can refuse wagers from states or provinces that prohibit sports wagering, and that bonuses are for US and Canada clients only. Its internet rules tell the client to decide whether the service is permitted where the client lives. Availability on a website is not permission. This page does not say JustBet is legal in any state or country.
